question.problem:
The function $f(x),$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3x+k}},\,x\ne -\frac{k}{3}
$$

has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{8}{3{x}^{3}}-\frac{5}{3},\,x\ne 0.
$$

What is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3x+k}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3y+k}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3y+k}} \\ \sqrt[3]{3y+k} & =\frac{2}{x} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{3y+k})}^{3} & ={(\frac{2}{x})}^{3} \\ 3y+k & =\frac{{2}^{3}}{{x}^{3}} \\ 3y & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}-k \\ 3y & =\frac{8}{{x}^{3}}-k \\ y & =\frac{8}{3{x}^{3}}-\frac{k}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{8}{3{x}^{3}}-\frac{k}{3},\,x\ne 0.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that

$$
-\frac{k}{3}=-\frac{5}{3}\,⟹\,k=5.
$$
